title: Radio show with Orson Welles blocked by Southern stations
summary: The Mobil Oil broadcast with Ethel Waters and Hall Johnson's choir was cut off by Southern stations.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I know one time we did a broadcast with -- is his name Orson Welles?

Yeah, it was radio then. Wasn't no TV. We did this thing. We had Hall Johnson's choir, one of the famous colored choirs in the world, famous. Ethel Waters, our band. We done this program for Mobil Oil. The Southern stations cut it off because we was colored. And it was one of the damnedest things you ever heard in your life because here's this big choir that sang. Oh, they sang, man. Something else. They were fabulous. Ethel Waters was at her peak then. She was beautiful. And our band put the icing on the cake. But they wouldn't play it on one of those Southern stations. I never got over it.

Mobil Oil. They wouldn't even play our records down home. Uh-uh. They play race records. Now, these other slobs, they'd play them all over the country and they ain't saying nothing. Country and Western, Nashville.
